title: How Do You Get the Attention of Museums? Lessons from Glass's Pioneers
author: Papi J
summary: Being a pioneer is about half the answer. Across two thousand years, the glassmakers who held museums' attention changed what glass can do, who can make it, what it can mean or where it can go — and almost all of them had an institution in the room early and left a record museums could find.

title: Blowing Glass in Lima
author: Glass Database
summary: Lima is an easy place to melt glass and a hard place to sell it — cheap piped gas, a mining economy that digs up every oxide in a glass batch, and a city of eleven million buying its glass from somewhere else. A hot shop here costs about $380,000 to build and $350,000 a year to run, and the constraint is not energy but demand.
